display.title: Episode 355: The Candle of the Neshamah and the Meaning of Asarah B'Teves
display.summary_short: After Chanukah, Uncle Yossi teaches how the neshamah stays lit with Torah and mitzvos, explains the fast of Asarah B'Teves, and shows how a pushka turns a whole house into a mitzvah.
display.summary_long: Broadcast the week after Chanukah 5749, five days before Asarah B'Teves. Uncle Yossi teaches that Chanukah is over but its light stays: the neshamah is Hashem's candle, mitzvos are the candle and Torah is the flame, and only together, with learning turned into action, do they give light. Like the menorah, a soldier of Tzivos Hashem shares his light with others. After the Hakochainik march, a brother and sister visiting from Ann Arbor, Michigan, lead the Shema. Then a look at the Jewish calendar: there is a time to be happy and a time to be sad, so that we learn from the past. On the tenth of Teves Nevuchadnetzar's army besieged Yerushalayim, leading to the breach of the walls on the seventeenth of Tammuz and the destruction of the Beis HaMikdash on Tisha B'Av. Torah and mitzvos are our protection, and Hashem promised to turn these fast days into Yomim Tovim; everyone calls out 'Ad mosai'. The show closes with how to make a mitzvah as big as your house: put up a tzedakah pushka.
display.lesson: Keep your neshamah shining with Torah and mitzvos all year, learn from the sad days of the past, and pray for Moshiach to turn them into days of joy.
